observations.body: Absalom acquires chariots and runners, intercepts those seeking judgment, presents himself as the judge they lack, asks leave for Hebron, sends spies, and gathers conspirators.

observations.body: The passage keeps Absalom, David, petitioners, spies, Ahithophel, and Israel, Jerusalem’s gate, Hebron, and all Israel, displaying, intercepting, touching, promising justice, asking leave, sending signals, and conspiring visible within David's story or later memory.

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 15:1–12 as its own exile, return, and rebellion David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places public accessibility becomes a path toward rival kingship inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
